text:
deploy-bot: rolling driver v525.85 + kernel 6.1.12 to a100 pool in us-west-2 (batch rollout 03/12 10:12 UTC)
anya: seeing a cluster alert spike, lots of P2P errors on a100 nodes in us-west-2 :eyes:
simon: confirmed. NCCL logs say P2P disabled, falling back to p2p=PCIe (no NVLink) for several pods — multi-gpu jobs time out or blow up memory
alex: perf impact huge — some training jobs 2-3x slower, queued pods failing with cudaMalloc or BAR1 mapping errors
infra-oncall: capturing logs, dmesg shows repeated lines: "nvidia 0000:81:00.0: BAR1 region too small" and "pci_enable_device: ACS not enabled, disabling peer access"
maria: quick checks: `nvidia-smi topo -m` on affected hosts shows NVLINK entries as "X" and P2P columns set to NO for some pairs
kevin: we did a kernel+driver rebase last night (kernel 6.1.12, cuda12.2, driver 525.85). prior stable was kernel 5.15 + driver 510.47
megan: any idea if this is driver change or kernel PCI subsystem? both teams need to know ASAP
anya: deploy-bot show: rollout started in us-west-2 -> 40 nodes -> 6 nodes flagged as degraded within 15m
alex: on a repro node I saw BAR1 size reported as 0x10000000 (256MB) when we expect ~2GB for BAR1 mappings. that causes large GPU memory mmaps to fail
simon: NCCL messages: "Channel p2p not available, falling back to unexpected topology" — causes extra copy hops and saturates PCIe root complex
infra-oncall: for mitigation we can: (1) pin new driver off canary nodes; (2) rollback driver on a small canary set; (3) if possible hot-patch kernel pci args. rolling back reduces capacity though
maria: customer comms in progress for impacted clusters, ops note: we may need to burst to cloud reserved pools to keep SLAs (cost hit estimated +20-30% if sustained)
kevin: starting rollback on a 6-node canary now (driver -> 510.47). will monitor NCCL test suite + nvlink topo
megan: any hotfix we can try before rollback? maybe module param or sysfs toggle?
anya: dev tested `echo 1 > /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/EnablePeerAccess` and `nvidia-smi --reset-gpu` restored peer access on one host, but that seems undocumented and fragile
simon: also saw suggestion to toggle ACS override on root port to re-enable peer access; that's invasive (requires rebind/reboot) and vendor support flagged as risky
alex: putting the quick check commands here:
```
# check topology
nvidia-smi topo -m
# check kernel/pci
dmesg | egrep -i "BAR1|ACS|peer|nvlink|p2p"
# check sysfs
cat /sys/module/nvidia/parameters/EnablePeerAccess || true
lspci -vvv | egrep -A5 "NVIDIA|Kernel driver in use"
```
infra-oncall: canary rollback in progress; if it heals we'll schedule staged rollback across remaining degraded nodes. will keep autoscaler paused for the pool to avoid scheduling churn
maria: ops note: bumped on-demand capacity in us-west-2 by 25% to absorb slowdowns — cost team notified, estimate +22% for the next 12h if not resolved
kevin: canary returned healthy after rollback on nodes a100-usw2-3..8 — NCCL tests passed, nvlink restored in topo output
megan: good, start rolling back staged. what's the plan for the rest of fleet? full rollback or vendor patch?
simon: filing kernel+driver ticket with vendor (tagging pci/acs, nvlink) — we need root cause. for now plan: full rollback for all affected pools, then run gradual re-roll with additional preflight tests (BAR1 sizing, nvlink topo, NCCL smoke)
anya: adding extra gate: require `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows NVLINK present and NCCL p2p smoke < 2s before widening rollout
kevin: opening rollback incident: INC-20250312-041, will link playbook and schedule after-hours window if needed
maria: posting dashboard links and customer impact list: https://internal.monitoring/r/ampere-p2p-20250312
alex: I'll draft a short postmortem template and assign action owners (driver gating, rollout preflight, cost mitigation)
megan: thanks all — keep threads brief in this channel, move long investigation notes to the incident doc
everyone: :thumbsup:
